This standard was first published in 1966. This standard has been revised to overcome encountered by the khadi industry in implementation of the standard. Following are the important changes carried out while revising this standard: in addition to four threads

difficulties

b) For checking the conformity of the sponge cloth to the requirements laid down in this standard a provision has been made for testing of the samples in prevailing atmospheric However, in case of dispute, the samples shall be tested after conditioning in conditions. the standard atmospheric conditions. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

TEXTILES - SPONGE CLOTH, COTTON KHADI, GREY - SPECIFICATION
( First Revision )
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes constructional particulars and other requirements of sponge cloth, cotton khadi, grey. 1.2 This standard does not appearance, feel, shade, etc. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standards listed at Annex A are necessary adjuncts to this standard. 3 ATMOSPHERIC TESTING CONDITIONS FOR specify the general neps and other spinning defects. The approximate count of warp and weft yarn is given in Table 1 4.2 Cloth The sponge cloth shall be woven in 2/2 twill weave. 4.2.1 The edges of sponge cloth shall be hemmed to a depth of not less than 15 mm with raw edges having a turn-in of 10 mm. The stitching shall be firm and regular. The hemming shall be uniform and flat and the edges shall be properly secured. 4.2.2 Two blue threads shall be running along the length of the sponge cloth at a distance of about 2.5 cm from each side. 4.2.3 The sponge cloth when visually examined, be reasonably free from spinning, weaving processing defects. 4.2.4 The selvedges well woven. 5 REQUIREMENTS 5.1 The constructional particulars of the sponge cloth shall conform to the requirements specified in Table 1. shall and

Test specimens may be conditioned and tested in the prevailing atmospheric conditions for checking the conformity of the cloth to the standard. However, in case of dispute, the specimens shall be conditioned and tested in the standard atmosphere as specified in the referred Indian Standards on test methods. 4 GENERAL 4.1 Yarn The yam used in the manufacture of sponge cloth shall be handspun from clean carded cotton. It shall be reasonably even and free from leaf particles, slubs, Table 1 Constructional REQUIREMENTS

METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF MASS PER PIECE

B-l Measure the length and width of each test specimen correct to the nearest 0.5 cm and determine its mass to nearest 5 g. Calculate the mass of each test specimen of dimensions specified m-5.2.

B-2 Report the lot to be in conformity with the requirement of Table 1 as regards mass per piece of sponge cloth, if the condition laid down in 8.4 is satisfied.
